transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-22
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Michael O'Brien (ArborTech CISO), Sana Khan (Head of Cloud Ops), Diego Ramirez (Privacy Counsel)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance review focused on: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/RBAC, audit log retention and immutability, KMS and HSM options, data residency, and Redwood's no-train-on-customer-data assurance plus prompt retention windows. Customer asked about PHI/PII flows and legal obligations (HIPAA context). Redwood clarified hosted vs private behavior and provided follow-ups.

Topics: SOC2, ISO27001, RBAC/SAML SSO, KMS (AWS + HSM), audit logs, data residency, no-training/no-fine-tune policy, prompt retention, deletion flows, HIPAA/PHI handling

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya our solutions eng. How are you all?
[00:05] Michael O'Brien: Good, thanks. Busy week but yeah we're ready.
[00:08] Sana Khan: Hi, thanks. We sent a calendar with the high level topics.
[00:11] Priya Raman: Great, thanks. I'll do the technical bits. Quick agenda check: we cover certs, SSO/RBAC, KMS, retention/no-train, and then open Qs. Does that work?
[00:20] Diego Ramirez: Works for me. We'll focus on legal/PII bits.

[02:10] Jordan Lee: To start, redwood's SOC 2 Type II attestation and ISO27001 status — we have active Type II for security and availability, and ISO27001 certified as of last quarter. I'll share the artifacts after the call. Note those include our control narratives and pen test summary.
[02:28] Michael O'Brien: When you say "share artifacts" is that an executive summary or the full report? We need an exec summary for procurement and the full attestation for our security audit team.
[02:34] Jordan Lee: Exec summary plus the signed attestation. We can't share raw internal logs but the attestation and scope statement are standard.

[04:12] Sana Khan: On SSO, we use SAML 2.0 with Okta. Do you support SCIM for provisioning and SAML for login? Also need role-based access control mapping to our LDAP groups.
[04:22] Priya Raman: Yes — we support SAML and SCIM. RBAC is group-mapped; you can map LDAP/Okta groups to roles (viewer, developer, admin). There's an audit trail for role changes. I'll provide the SCIM schema and examples.
[04:36] Michael O'Brien: How granular are the audit logs? Are they immutable? We need to show change history for at least 12 months.
[04:44] Priya Raman: Audit logs capture API calls, role changes, user invites, model rollouts, and admin actions. They're write-once in our log store and we provide 90 days by default in hosted. For enterprise dedicated/private you can configure longer retention — we support up to multi-year in the Private deployment with customer-managed S3 or your SIEM.
[05:05] Diego Ramirez: For compliance we need immutability proof and a notarized chain? That's more than a standard ask.
[05:12] Jordan Lee: Understood — for Private we can point you to options: WORM-enabled S3 buckets and integration with your SIEM for forwarding. We'll include the architecture note in the docs.

[07:30] Sana Khan: KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys and HSMs. Can Redwood integrate with external HSM or bring-your-own-key?
[07:38] Priya Raman: Yes. Two options: hosted with Redwood-managed KMS (customer data encrypted at rest with keys we manage) or customer-managed KMS where you provide AWS KMS keys or via a CloudHSM/HSM gateway. In Private, you own the keys and we don't have access to the plaintext. We'll share a runbook for both.
[07:55] Michael O'Brien: Do tokens/temporary keys for inference get decrypted on your side? I'm trying to understand if any keys ever leave our control.
[08:02] Priya Raman: For customer-managed KMS, the keys never leave your account; Redwood services call KMS in your control plane. In hosted mode with customer KMS we still do the crypto operations in our runtime but keys are in your KMS — Redwood holds no plaintext key material.

[10:20] Diego Ramirez: About training: we need a contractual assurance that customer prompts and outputs are not used to train or improve models. Can you confirm?
[10:28] Jordan Lee: Short answer: yes. Redwood does not train on customer-provided prompts or responses by default. We have a strict policy: no training or fine-tuning on customer traffic unless there's an explicit, opt-in agreement that is documented.
[10:40] Michael O'Brien: Is that in the standard agreement or a separate addendum? We need legal language.
[10:44] Jordan Lee: It's available as an addendum — "No Training on Customer Data" — and we'll send the exact contractual language. We'll also show audit logs that indicate data paths.
[11:03] Sana Khan: Does that also apply to aggregated telemetry? Some vendors claim they anonymize and aggregate for telemetry.
[11:10] Priya Raman: Telemetry for service health (e.g., latency, error rates, model performance) is collected and aggregated, but we don't feed customer prompt text into model training pipelines. We can also offer telemetry redaction options.

[12:45] Michael O'Brien: Prompt retention — what's the default retention window for prompts and completions? Our concern is PHI accidentally appearing and retention rules.
[12:53] Priya Raman: Hosted default: ephemeral prompt retention for 30 days for debugging/quality only, then deleted. You can request shorter retention in contract (e.g., 0 days or 7 days). In Private you control retention entirely. We also support on-request deletion APIs and legal hold flags.
[13:22] Diego Ramirez: You mentioned ephemeral — is deletion immediate for hosted if we call the deletion API?
[13:27] Priya Raman: Deletion APIs mark data for deletion; we perform secure deletion according to our policy — usually within 24–72 hours to allow background processes to complete. For stricter needs, Private deployment is recommended. We'll document SLOs.

[15:01] Sana Khan: Data residency: we need EU-only processing for a subset of customers. Can Redwood pin model serving to eu-west-1 and ensure data never leaves the region?
[15:09] Priya Raman: Yes — we support region pinning. For hosted we have regions in NA, EU and APAC. Policy-based routing pins traffic to a region and we have controls to prevent cross-region fallbacks for data residency constraints. For strict requirements we recommend Private in your VPC.

[17:40] Michael O'Brien: HIPAA: Are you willing to sign a BAA?
[17:44] Jordan Lee: Redwood can sign a BAA for customers that need HIPAA compliance, provided we run in a compliant deployment mode (Dedicated or Private) and configuration meets BAA controls. We'll follow up with the legal team on standard BAA terms.

[19:55] Diego Ramirez: Auditability: we want a trail that ties a given prompt to user ID and request ID. Is that available?
[20:03] Priya Raman: Yes, logs include request_id, user_id (if available from your identity header), model version, timestamp, and route. For hosted we can surface these in the Console and export them to your SIEM. For extra security we can hash identifiers so that you get linkage while minimizing exposure.

[23:30] Sana Khan: Can we configure tokenization/redaction at the SDK level so we never send PHI to Redwood? We're exploring client-side redaction.
[23:37] Priya Raman: Definitely — we offer SDK hooks for client-side redaction and a local sanitizer library that can be deployed in your edge before calls reach Redwood. That is the recommended pattern if you want zero PHI ever transmitted.

[25:10] Michael O'Brien: In the case we do need to pass PHI for a use case, is there a recommended hardened path?
[25:17] Priya Raman: Yes: Private deployment with customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and retention set to minimal/zero plus restricted RBAC and dedicated capacity. That meets the typical HIPAA stack. We'll provide a checklist.

[27:05] Jordan Lee: A quick note on model variants and fallbacks — if your route is pinned to a region and primary model is unavailable, by default we fallback to a compatible model which might be in another region; we can override that behavior for customers requiring strict residency.
[27:22] Sana Khan: We need that override.
[27:25] Jordan Lee: Noted.

[29:40] Diego Ramirez: Regarding deletion proofs — can you provide an audit record showing deletion actions and who initiated them?
[29:47] Priya Raman: Yes, deletion events are logged with actor, timestamp, and request_id. For Private setups, those logs are under customer control and can be forwarded to your SIEM.

[32:18] Michael O'Brien: For encryption in transit, do you support mTLS between our VPC and Redwood endpoints?
[32:24] Priya Raman: Yes, mTLS is supported for Private connections. For hosted we use TLS 1.2/1.3 with strong ciphers. mTLS is part of the Private deployment runbook.

[34:50] Sana Khan: Are there any third parties who have access to raw customer prompts (e.g., for debugging)?
[34:57] Jordan Lee: No standard third-party access. For critical production debugging, customers can opt in to session sharing with engineered redaction and only under NDA. Otherwise we provide logs and metrics; we don't share raw prompts with external vendors.

[36:10] Diego Ramirez: Pen test cadence?
[36:13] Jordan Lee: We do annual external penetration tests and quarterly internal scans. We'll share a redacted pen test executive summary.

[38:30] Michael O'Brien: SLA and incident response — in the event of a security incident involving customer data, what's the notification SLA?
[38:37] Jordan Lee: We have a 24-hour initial notification SLA for confirmed incidents affecting customer data, and follow our incident response playbook with triage, timeline, and mitigations. For Dedicated/Private, SLA terms are contractually specified.

[40:55] Sana Khan: A couple of nitty gritty: retention windows per environment, ability to pull raw logs for forensics, and support window for KMS rotation.
[41:05] Priya Raman: Retention by default: hosted logs 90 days, prompts 30 days; Dedicated configurable to 1-3 years; Private you control. Raw logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM for forensics. KMS rotation: supports automatic rotation and manual rotation; we have a rekey window approach to avoid request failures — we'll include rotation guidance.

[43:30] Diego Ramirez: One more legal ask: sample contract clause for "No training/no model improvement" and the deletion SLAs.
[43:37] Jordan Lee: We'll attach sample clauses and the addendum.

[45:10] Michael O'Brien: That covers our high-level concerns. Next you send docs, Priya builds the KMS runbook, and we schedule the private deep dive.
[45:18] Jordan Lee: Yep. We'll get those over. Thanks everyone.
[46:00] Sana Khan: Thanks. Quick note, Diego and I will sync offline about the PHI list.
[46:06] Diego Ramirez: Yep.
[47:30] Jordan Lee: End of call.

Call artifacts referenced (links to be provided): SOC2 attestation PDF, ISO27001 cert, pen test exec summary, KMS integration runbook (draft), Private deployment checklist, sample contract no-train addendum.

Transcript notes: occasional filler words removed for readability; some Speaker labels approximated by the transcription engine; references to internal product names might be slightly off (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache in one capture).
